executive_brief: The Enhanced Expense Tracker is a single-user local financial application centered on a structured data model for expenditure tracking. It implements a CRUD-based persistence layer where each expense record is governed by strict validation rules regarding monetary values, date formatting, and categorized spending. The system operates on a local storage pattern with a implicit 1:N relationship between the local user and expense entities.

architectural_constraints: Amount must be strictly > 0; values <= 0 must trigger a ValidationError
Date must strictly match the YYYY-MM-DD regex (ISO 8601)
Category must be one of the following case-sensitive strings: Food, Transport, Bills, Utilities
Description must be of type string (nullable/empty allowed)
Primary Key for expenses must be an AUTOINCREMENT INTEGER
Created_at field must be managed by the database via DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP

maturity_assessment: The project is currently in a REFINEMENT state. While the data model is logically complete with a 100% completeness score for the extracted entities, it suffers from significant structural gaps. Specifically, the absence of high-priority business goals and non-functional requirements regarding performance and security creates a lack of architectural context, necessitating further specification before full-scale implementation.
critical_dependencies: Implicit 1:N relationship between local user context and ENT-EXPENSE entity
Database engine supporting SQLite-style PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
